html:
SMTO-RST-0011 — SMTO can't continue this task because some earlier results are gone

GUID: b0d65691-8c35-403b-a770-5ada0f341fb7
Slug: resume-evidence-unavailable
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to continue a task, but some results saved by the earlier attempt are no longer stored. SMTO did not start the new attempt, so nothing new ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the stopped task and read its last messages and results to see which steps it already finished, without making another change. The earlier attempt may already have changed files or systems, and repeating those steps could do them twice.
  2. Check the actual files, messages or systems the task was working on to confirm what is already done. SMTO lost part of the earlier results, so the real state outside SMTO is the only reliable record.
  3. Start a new task in the same conversation that asks SMTO to look at the current state first and only do the work still missing. A new task does not need the lost results, so it can go ahead without guessing what happened before.
  4. Keep the original conversation and task; don't delete them to make room for the new one. They still hold the record of what the earlier attempt did.

What success looks like

  • The new task starts, reports what it found already done, and finishes only the remaining work.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the conversation or the saved data folder; they hold the earlier results.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Continuation creation stopped because a result reference carried from the source run has no retained artifact record (native_artifacts) for its origin run.

What this means

  • Continuation creation cannot locate the retained evidence required by its original source run. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Continuation creation cannot locate the retained evidence required by its original source run.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the source run's retained artifacts/receipts and storage ownership before creating another continuation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the source run's results and historical_results refs against native_artifacts and native_artifact_links for the origin run; the referenced artifact was purged or never committed. Keep the source run, restore the artifact only through supported recovery, otherwise start a new task that re-inspects the current external state read-only instead of replaying earlier work.
  • Keep the source run and inspect its retained evidence storage. If evidence cannot be restored through supported means, begin a new read-only inspection of current external state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Required original evidence is available, or new inspection establishes current external state without replay.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
